purpose: Public output-quality cases, all previously exposed; not a new sealed holdout. Expected answers/checks are evaluator-only.

evals.prompt:
I'm making a Bitcoin Script exercise. Write script.asm that consumes two initial
stack integers, adds them, and leaves true exactly when their sum is 16. For
other sums it must finish successfully leaving one false item. Use btcdeb
to demonstrate two different satisfying inputs and one non-satisfying input.
Save result.json with {"tested": true} after the actual runs, plus a short explanation.
evals.expected_output: A Script accepting sums of16, two satisfying executions, one false result, requested JSON and explanation.
assertions: Deliver the artifacts and machine-readable fields explicitly requested in the prompt.
Support operation claims with actual tool execution; explain the central observed outcome accurately.
Saved Script satisfies the declared execution vectors, including their false/error boundaries.

evals.prompt:

flow restores every internal state; this exercise specifically checks undoing
a stack push.

"final_stack_hex": [...], "rewind_restored_previous_state": boolean} and explain
the observations. I want a real debugging session, not just a predicted trace.

assertions: Deliver the artifacts and machine-readable fields explicitly requested in the prompt.
